ca_oven_the.blurb: The Oven is a small sport wall tucked into the Big Chief zone above the Truckee River Canyon, near Lake Tahoe, at roughly 7,000 feet. It holds ten bolted lines, with one at 5.9, four at 5.10, three at 5.11, and a pair of hard 5.12 and 5.13 test pieces at the top end, so it suits someone who already leads 5.10 comfortably more than a beginner. The wall takes plenty of direct sun, which makes cooler days the better choice, and it sees noticeably fewer parties than the busier faces next door even though it sits close to the main trail in.

ca_kindergarten_rock.blurb: Kindergarten Rock is a broken, fairly large outcrop in the Children's Forest cluster on Keller Peak, in the San Bernardino Mountains above Running Springs, at about 7,100 feet. It carries ten routes in a friendly spread, from 5.5 up to 5.11, mixing five trad lines with three bolted routes and two top-rope problems. The moderate cracks and faces are on the east side, and the base sits beside a seasonal creek. Overhead power lines make the rock easy to pick out as you hike in, and the walk takes around ten to fifteen minutes. A decent choice for newer leaders who also want a few harder options.

ca_handlebar_boulder.blurb: Handlebar Boulder is a riverside bouldering spot in the Bar section of Auburn State Recreation Area, west of the Sierra foothills at a low elevation of about 590 feet. It has ten problems, about twelve feet tall at most, with a strong tilt toward the middle and upper end: a few V3 and V4 lines, then several V6 and V7 problems for strong climbers. Among the Bar boulders it is one of the better-trafficked, so expect company. You reach it by dropping off the main trail past the path toward Shogun and following a faint track through light forest to a small clearing above the river.

ca_headbangers_cave.blurb: Headbangers Cave is a compact bouldering alcove inside the Happy Boulders, north of Bishop in the Eastern Sierra, at about 4,500 feet. It is among the first spots on the hike up from the parking lot: pass the Jesus Chrysler Boulder, then peel right onto a short spur trail. Easy to walk straight by if you hurry. Its ten problems are short, steep and over a good landing, mostly V1 to V3 with a handful of V4 to V6 climbs and one very hard V9 at the top. Loose rock in the neighbourhood means topping out deserves some care.
